q684a09a1.question: A legacy review comment can target a companion file (target.file other than the artifact's own document, for example a diagram or mock) while the Feedback shape has an anchor but no file: should such a comment be stored on the companion's own DIAG artifact when one exists, kept on the parent artifact with the file path in anchor.section, or have its file dropped?
q684a09a1.choice: Keep on the parent artifact with the file path in anchor.section
q684a09a1.rationale: No DIAG lookup; the file is not lost and the thread stays on the artifact the person reviewed.

q937a3db7.question: The legacy kind 'feedback' (a request to change the artifact) has no direct match: should it be stored as revision-request, as comment, or by the decision it came with (send-feedback to revision-request, approve and reject to comment)?
q937a3db7.choice: By the decision that took effect (feedback to revision-request, approve and reject to comment)
q937a3db7.rationale: A withheld approval records its comments under the feedback decision, which is a request to change the artifact; the legacy IPC kind feedback maps to revision-request.

qb737f0d4.question: The readers of body.feedback (companion headers, delivery) will show only entries written before s5 until the s9 conversion, while new feedback is in the line files: should s5 add the line-file entries to those readers, or leave the mixed view until s9?
qb737f0d4.choice: Leave the mixed view until s9
qb737f0d4.rationale: The readers switch with the conversion; s5 adds no reader changes.

q395feeb8.question: ep3: the invariants name the capability ids c1 to c5 whose citations point at the s1 bundles, but they do not quote the bundle text
q395feeb8.rationale: The citations point at the s1 bundles; a documentation gap covered by the LLD approval override.

summary.prose: Story s5 lets a person add feedback or a reply on any artifact, a Task included, and see what is still open. Every entry is one immutable line with a namespaced author, the time and the artifact revision it was made against; a reply is its own line that names its parent, and a revision of the artifact addresses all open feedback unless its author lists only some. A per-user identity file links a person's several accounts for display, while the gates keep deciding on the tracker's own identity.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Chosen framework (a1): a shared artifact envelope with typed payloads, stored as a head file plus two append-only sidecar files whose lines carry the owning artifact id, behind a single identity module, with one upfront conversion and no compatibility code. The envelope carries identity, description, parent, references, a typed lifecycle (revision, approval, review, signoffs, staleness, status) and a tracker binding or attachments; the change log and feedback are separate append-only line files; each existing artifact type shrinks to a payload codec and a renderer. Tracker comment reading and attaching are added to the port and implemented for the GitHub adapter only.

consumedContracts.name: ArtifactIdScheme
consumedContracts.purpose: The single place artifact ids are made and recognised: the existing hierarchical typed ids extended for Epic, Story, Task, the Tasks file and diagrams, one story and task form, the folder-name date source, and the functional-requirement id helpers that live in id.ts today.

consumedContracts.name: ArtifactEnvelope
consumedContracts.purpose: The common shape of every stored entity and the one reader and writer for it, with References and namespaced Actors.

consumedContracts.name: HistoryRecords
consumedContracts.purpose: The change log entry and the Feedback entry shapes, the persisted sidecar record that carries the owning artifact id, and the append and read API, including how an update says which feedback it addressed.

consumedContracts.name: SidecarStorage
consumedContracts.purpose: How an artifact is stored: the head file and the two append-only line files shared by a Tasks file, their location, the merge rule, the per-artifact filtering and the read-time ordering and de-duplication.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface ArtifactFiles { head: string; log: string; feedback: string }
interface SidecarStore { filesOf(id: string): ArtifactFiles; appendRecord<E>(file: string, record: SidecarRecord<E>): Promise<void>; readRecords<E>(file: string, artifactId: string): Promise<E[]>; mergeAttributes(): string[] }

boundary.internal: People-facing feedback: adding feedback and replies from a client, listing open feedback, the addresses rule at revision time, and the per-user identity declaration with alias linking. Private to this Story are the identity file format and the display of linked identities.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The id module and its removal of the second scheme: the folder-name formatter moved into the path scheme, the date source fixed to the epic's creation time, the functional-requirement id helpers and their callers moved with stored FR ids staying valid, issue titles switched to the artifact id, and the delivery module's ordinals. The old issue-body marker is not read. Private to this Story are the exact text of the issue title and the relocation of the helpers.

The envelope model, the one reader and writer, the History API and the sidecar record shape as a contract, and the repository version marker. Private to this Story are the head-file schema, the per-type payload codec registry and how the old per-type read functions delegate to the reader.

The lifecycle rules: status transitions, the revision and content-hash computation, the staleness record, the completion roll-up and the integrity check against the log tail on approve, review and complete. Private to this Story are the hash canonicalisation and how a roll-up is cached or recomputed.

The physical sidecar storage: file layout, the merge attributes for the line files, per-artifact filtering, read-time ordering and de-duplication, and the write order of log entry before head with the repair of a log that is ahead of its head. Private to this Story are the line format and the file naming beside a head.

The typed binding and attachments, the tracker port additions implemented for GitHub, the retry of pending links and posts, and the switch of unit-issue bookkeeping to the binding. Private to this Story are the permalink construction and the retry bookkeeping.

Task artifacts: creation of the Tasks file and the Task issues at plan approval, direct edits of a Task's own content with local re-approval, refusal of structural edits, and the re-plan reconciliation. Private to this Story are the diff of a Task against the new plan and the build-round recording in a Task's history.

Comment sync: reading human comments into feedback at implement, validate or on request, classifying a revision request or a suggestion from the first line, and posting feedback once. Private to this Story are the first-line commands, the derived since point and the filter for the framework's own posts.

The conversion command: previews, repeats, back-fills history, renames standalone S001 to s1 rewriting the references it can with no alias, creates Epic, Story and Task artifacts for what exists, verifies through the delivery reader, and sets the repository version. Private to this Story are the per-type conversion mappings and the verification report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase C — feedback and tracker binding

nonFunctional.performance: Reading an artifact reads its head; the log tail is read only on approve, review and complete, and counts, open feedback and status are computed on read. The delivery loader still reads each artifact once. Loading a repository of about a thousand artifacts must stay within twice today's load time on the same machine.
nonFunctional.security: Gates use the live tracker identity only; declared aliases are never trusted for a decision. The identity file is local and read for attribution. Tracker comments are read through the existing gh path of the GitHub adapter, with no new credential and no direct REST call.
nonFunctional.observability: Every state change appends a change log entry with actor, operation and, where relevant, revision and status; a conflict, a log-ahead-of-head repair, a failed attach and a pending link are logged and surfaced in the unit's result, not hidden.
nonFunctional.durability: Heads are replaced atomically as today; sidecar lines are append-only and de-duplicated by (artifactId, entry id) so a repeated append is harmless; a write appends its log entry before it replaces the head so a failure between the two leaves a detectable, repairable gap; the conversion is one commit, repeatable, and reverts with one git revert.

dataModelChanges.details: Adds optional inReplyTo: string (a root entry's id). A reply is a separate line with feedback: []. Ids are minted as 32 hex characters (a uuid without dashes), or taken from the caller's id; validateFeedback rejects an inReplyTo equal to the entry's own id. Everything else is the s2 shape.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: interface Feedback { ...; readonly inReplyTo?: string | undefined }

dataModelChanges.details: An update entry whose revision number is higher than the previous entry's carries addresses 'all' unless the writer gave a list; a lifecycle operation or an update with no revision change carries none and addresses nothing. This is the Gap 5 rule that open feedback is whatever no later update addressed.
A read-time view, never stored: { root: Feedback; replies: Feedback[]; addressed: boolean; addressedBy?: string; orphan?: boolean }.
~/.insrc/identity.json, { primary: string; aliases: string[] }, every id namespaced and lower-case. Self-declared, local to the machine, used for attribution and display only. Private to this Story.

When an actor is recorded, the declared aliases are copied into properties.aliases only when the actor's id is the declared primary or one of the aliases; a linked id never makes one actor stand for another in any decision.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Uses History.appendFeedback, feedback and openFeedback and the ChangeLogEntry.addresses field; asks for one additive field (inReplyTo) through the amendment above.
Reads and appends feedback through the SidecarStore (filesOf, appendRecord, readRecords) as built by s4; a Task's feedback lands in its Story's Tasks file and is filtered by artifact id.
Reads the head through ArtifactStore.read (existence and current revision) and uses readWithHistory for the combined view; Actor is the sc2 shape.
Validates and classifies artifact ids with ArtifactIds.parse (a TASK id maps to its Tasks file).

errorCases.scenario: Feedback is added to a Task whose artifact does not exist yet
errorCases.detection: ArtifactStore.read(artifactId) raises ArtifactNotFoundError before any line is appended
errorCases.response: FeedbackService.add rethrows it; nothing is written
errorCases.userImpact: A person gets 'no such artifact'; a Task takes feedback once the plan approval creates its artifact (s7)

errorCases.scenario: A reply names a parent that is missing, belongs to another artifact, or is itself a reply
errorCases.detection: add reads the artifact's feedback and looks the inReplyTo id up among root entries
errorCases.response: HistoryEntryError naming the id; nothing is appended
errorCases.userImpact: The reply is refused with the reason; the person re-sends it against the thread's root

errorCases.scenario: A retried add with the same caller id but different text
errorCases.detection: the sidecar reader sees one (artifactId, id) with two contents and raises HistoryReadError; add checks the stored entry for the id before appending
errorCases.response: HistoryEntryError 'id already used with different content'; the first entry stays as stored
errorCases.userImpact: The client learns its key was reused; the original entry is intact

errorCases.scenario: A process dies after the line is appended but before the caller sees the result, and the client retries with the same id
errorCases.detection: add finds an identical stored entry for the id
errorCases.response: returns the stored entry and appends nothing
errorCases.userImpact: No duplicate; the retry returns the first result

errorCases.scenario: A revision lists feedback ids in addresses that are not roots of this artifact, or were addressed by an earlier revision
errorCases.detection: ArtifactStore.write reads the artifact's feedback and its earlier update entries before staging
errorCases.response: HistoryEntryError listing the unknown ids; nothing is staged and the head is unchanged
errorCases.userImpact: The revision is refused and says which ids are wrong

errorCases.scenario: The identity file is present but is not valid JSON, or holds an id that is not namespaced and lower-case
errorCases.detection: IdentityService.show parses and validates the file
errorCases.response: IdentityError naming the file and the problem; currentActor logs it and records the actor without aliases, so feedback is never blocked by the file
errorCases.userImpact: Attribution continues with no links; show and declare report the problem

errorCases.scenario: The tracker does not answer whoAmI (not signed in, offline, no tracker)
errorCases.detection: PortResult is not ok, or the tracker cannot be loaded
errorCases.response: currentActor falls back to git:<email>, then os:<user>@<host>; the fallback and the reason are logged
errorCases.userImpact: The entry is recorded under a git or OS identity; gates are unaffected because they never read this

errorCases.scenario: A request names an actor that is not a namespaced lower-case id
errorCases.detection: approvalActorOf and the add path's actor check
errorCases.response: the request is refused with the id it received; nothing is recorded
errorCases.userImpact: The client fixes the id; no entry is attributed to a guessed identity

errorCases.scenario: The review decision stored the approval but saving its comments through the service fails
errorCases.detection: handleReviewDecision catches the add error after the decision took effect
errorCases.response: the result reports commentsError exactly as it does now; the decision stays
errorCases.userImpact: The approval stands and the person is told the comments were not saved

errorCases.scenario: Two clones add feedback to one artifact and are merged
errorCases.detection: the feedback file is merge=union; the reader dedupes by (artifactId, id)
errorCases.response: both sets of lines are read once each, ordered by time then id; two different entries that picked the same caller id are a HistoryReadError on read
errorCases.userImpact: Both people's feedback appears; a true id clash is reported, not hidden

edgeCases.expected: refused: threads are one level deep, so the reply is made against the root (the nested feedback[] of the s2 shape stays for tracker-ingested entries)

edgeCases.input: A revision that changes no content (an identical rewrite)
edgeCases.expected: writes nothing, so nothing is addressed and all feedback stays open

edgeCases.input: A revision with addresses as an empty list
edgeCases.expected: valid: it addresses nothing, every root stays open

edgeCases.input: A lifecycle operation such as approve or review
edgeCases.expected: its log entry has no addresses; approval does not resolve feedback

edgeCases.input: A reply added after its root was addressed
edgeCases.expected: stored; the thread stays addressed because the reply carries no state, and a later revision does not need to address it

edgeCases.input: A person whose github id is the declared primary and whose jira id is an alias adds feedback
edgeCases.expected: recorded as github:<login> with properties.aliases [jira:<id>]; a different person's actor never receives these aliases

edgeCases.input: Feedback with the same timestamp as the update that addresses it
edgeCases.expected: ordered by the shared (timestamp, id) rule: the update addresses it only when its id sorts after the feedback's
the line goes to the Story's TASKS feedback file with the TASK id as artifactId, and is read back for that Task only

invariantsToPreserve.text: A stored feedback line is never edited or removed: the service has no edit or delete call and appendRecord is the only writer of the file
A repeated append of the same (artifactId, id) with the same content is harmless, and with different content is corruption the reader reports (s4's rule is not weakened)
Gates decide on TrackerPort.whoAmI only; nothing under src/workflow/team imports the identity module or reads the identity file
A revision moves only when content changes (k3); addressing feedback and adding feedback never move it
Open feedback is derived from the log, never stored on an entry, and uses the shared (timestamp, id) order so the feedback and log files agree whichever is read first
The legacy body.feedback writers and readers keep working until s9 retires them; s5 adds no compatibility code for them

migration.stateBefore: Feedback reaches an artifact only as body.feedback in its head JSON, written by appendFeedback and appendFeedbackBatch (the daemon's artifact.feedback.append and the review decision), with a plain-name author, no replies, no revision-request kind and no addresses. The sidecar History.appendFeedback exists (s2) over the durable line files (s4) but nothing in production calls it; no namespaced actor is built for a person and no identity file exists. Gates decide on TrackerPort.whoAmI.
migration.stateAfter: A FeedbackService over History records feedback and replies on any artifact, a Task included, as immutable framed lines with a namespaced actor; every revision addresses open feedback by default or by list; an identity service builds the person's actor and reads the local identity file for display only; the daemon's feedback add and list, identity show and declare, the artifact.feedback.append handler and the review decision's comments all go through the service. Gates are unchanged. Entries already in body.feedback stay where they are until s9 converts them.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional inReplyTo field to the Feedback shape and its validation in History, and file the sc3 amendment; no stored line changes
Apply the addresses rule in the store: stamp 'all' on an update that moves the revision, validate listed ids; existing update entries without addresses are read as addressing nothing, as before
Add the feedback module (service, thread view) and the identity module with its local file, unused by any caller yet
Give the registry entry a FeedbackService and add the daemon methods for feedback add and list and for identity show and declare

Point artifact.feedback.append and the review decision's comments at the service for every artifact the registry can read; the legacy body.feedback writers stay in place for callers outside the daemon and for tests

Record in the plans document what s9 must do with body.feedback entries (convert them into feedback lines with a synthesised actor and kind) and that the readers of body.feedback show only old entries until then

migration.backwardCompat: No compatibility code is added, by the owner's ruling for this branch. The only existing public surfaces are the daemon's artifact.feedback.append request, which keeps its request shape and now stores a Feedback line (its author string becomes the actor name when no actor id is given, its kind 'feedback' is stored as revision-request), and the review decision's request and result, whose entryIds are now Feedback ids. Callers of the legacy writers outside the daemon keep working unchanged. Entries already written to body.feedback are not read by the new service and not rewritten until the s9 conversion.

alternativesConsidered.name: Feedback service, flat lines with inReplyTo, one identity module
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A FeedbackService over History records entries and replies as flat immutable lines (a reply names its parent in a new inReplyTo field), a thread view nests them at read, and an identity module builds namespaced actors; the production feedback writers move onto it.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new feedback module (service plus pure thread builder) sits on History and the s4 registry. add(artifactId, input, actor) checks the artifact exists, the actor is namespaced, a reply's parent exists on the same artifact and is not itself a reply, mints the id and the time, validates through History.appendFeedback and returns the stored entry; there is no edit or delete call. Because a stored line can never be rewritten, a reply is its own line carrying inReplyTo (the parent's id); this needs one added optional field on the sc3 Feedback shape, filed as an amendment to the HLD and validated by History.validateFeedback, and threads(artifactId) nests replies under parents at read (the stored feedback[] stays empty for new lines, so the s2 shape and its recursion still hold for tracker-ingested entries s8 may write). open(artifactId) is History.openFeedback, ordered by the shared (timestamp, id) rule; the addresses of a revision are chosen by the author when the content update is recorded (LifecycleService.updateContent and ArtifactStore.update take an addresses option, default 'all'; a list leaves the rest open, and a list naming an unknown id is refused). An identity module reads ~/.insrc/identity.json ({ primary, aliases[] }, self-declared, attribution only), builds Actors (github:<login> from the tracker's whoAmI, git:<email>, os:<user>@<host> as fallbacks) with the declared aliases copied into properties.aliases, and exposes declare/show; gates keep calling the tracker's whoAmI directly and never read the file. The daemon gets IPC methods to add, list and declare, and artifact.feedback.append and the review decision's comments are re-pointed at the service for every artifact the registry can store, the legacy body.feedback reader staying until s9.
pros: One feedback path for every artifact kind, a Task included, with replies, kinds and revision requests as ac14 asks
Immutability is structural: the only write is an append and the API has no edit
Identity and gates are separated by construction, so a declared alias cannot spoof a claim (ac16)
Moving the production writers now means the board and the review pane see one history instead of two
cons: Needs a sc3 amendment (inReplyTo) to a shape s2 owns, and an approved HLD amendment before the plan
The re-pointed writers change the review decision's feedback path and its tests
Legacy readers of body.feedback show only old entries until s9 back-fills, so a mixed view exists for a while

alternativesConsidered.name: New path only, legacy writers untouched until s9
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The same service, thread view and identity module, but artifact.feedback.append and the review decision keep writing body.feedback, so new feedback calls are the only users of the sidecar.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Build the FeedbackService, the thread builder and the identity module as in a1 (same inReplyTo amendment, same addresses option, same identity file), expose them through new IPC methods, and leave the legacy appendFeedback and appendFeedbackBatch writers, their IPC and the review pane's comment saving exactly as they are; s9's conversion later moves old entries into the line files and retires body.feedback and its writers together.
pros: Smallest change to running behaviour: no existing caller or test of the legacy writers moves
The conversion in s9 already has to rewrite those entries, so nothing is migrated twice
Easy to ship and to revert
cons: Two feedback stores live side by side, so 'see what is still open' on one artifact needs both and an artifact can show comments in only one of them
Review-pane comments, the most used feedback today, still carry a bare name and no identity or replies, so ac14 and ac16 hold only for callers of the new path
A person's new feedback and the review pane's feedback on the same artifact are ordered by no common rule
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cheapest and safest to ship, but it leaves the most used feedback path outside ac14 to ac16 and leaves two stores for s9 to reconcile, which the acceptance criteria say should be one.

alternativesConsidered.name: Replies stored inside the parent, merged at read
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A reply is appended as a new line with the parent's id and the reply in feedback[], and the reader merges lines that share an id into one thread, so no new Feedback field is needed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep the sc3 Feedback shape exactly as s2 shipped it. add() of a top-level entry appends one line; a reply appends a second line with the SAME id and text as the parent and a feedback[] holding the reply, and the sidecar reader (s4's sc5) merges lines with the same (artifactId, entry id) by concatenating their feedback[] instead of treating different content as a conflict; the thread view is then the merged list. The identity module and the addresses option are as in a1.
pros: No amendment to the Feedback shape
Replies literally nest under the parent as the settled Gap 5 wording says
cons: Reverses s4's rule that a repeated id with different content is corruption, so a real conflict (a hand-edited or merged line) can no longer be told from a reply
The stored parent line is no longer the immutable entry ac14 describes: its meaning changes as lines are added
Reaches into sc5, which s4 owns, so it needs a second amendment and a change to the framed reader and its tests
A union merge of two clones adding replies to one parent depends on the merge of identical parent text
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Avoids a new field by weakening the integrity rule of the storage s4 built; it violates ac14, k4 and the ownership of sc5.

openQuestions: ep3: the invariants name the capability ids c1 to c5 whose citations point at the s1 bundles, but they do not quote the bundle text

A legacy review comment can target a companion file (target.file other than the artifact's own document, for example a diagram or mock) while the Feedback shape has an anchor but no file: should such a comment be stored on the companion's own DIAG artifact when one exists, kept on the parent artifact with the file path in anchor.section, or have its file dropped?

The legacy kind 'feedback' (a request to change the artifact) has no direct match: should it be stored as revision-request, as comment, or by the decision it came with (send-feedback to revision-request, approve and reject to comment)?

The readers of body.feedback (companion headers, delivery) will show only entries written before s5 until the s9 conversion, while new feedback is in the line files: should s5 add the line-file entries to those readers, or leave the mixed view until s9?

erDefinition.narrative: A thread is a root feedback line with the reply lines that name it; an update log entry addresses roots; an identity file links a person's accounts to the actors that are recorded.

Feedback.description: One immutable feedback line on an artifact.

inReplyTo.description: The root entry this replies to; absent on a root.

actor.description: Who wrote it, with a namespaced id.

revision.description: The artifact revision it was made against.

ChangeLogEntry.description: A log line; an update names the feedback roots it addresses.

addresses.description: 'all' or the root ids this revision addresses.

Actor.description: A person, agent or system with a namespaced id.

aliases.description: Declared ids of the same person, for display only.

IdentityFile.description: The per-user local declaration of a person's ids.
